findings.problem: Direct comparison against the held primary witnesses and against sections/30-detailed-commentary.tex:70-75 shows that the rewritten opening of Interpretation 3 conflates St. Bede and St. Gregory the Great so that each Father is credited with a Gospel passage and exegetical argument he does not make: (1) line 4 writes 'St. Bede and St. Gregory the Great distinguish clerical and lay watchfulness and map the night watches onto the ages of human life,' whereas St. Bede (In Marci Evangelium Expositio IV.13, latin-text-b8197766 lines 402-405) distinguishes clerical (janitor = pastors) and lay watchfulness but never maps the night watches onto the ages of human life, while St. Gregory the Great (Homiliae in Evangelia, Hom. 13 on Luke 12:35-40, complete-extracted-text-dc25dd69 lines 139-145) maps the three Lucan night watches onto boyhood, youth, and old age but never distinguishes clerical (janitor) and lay watchfulness; (2) line 8 writes 'St. Bede (In Marci Evangelium Expositio IV.13) and St. Gregory the Great (Homiliae in Evangelia, Homilies 9 and 13) read the household of Mark 13:34 as the ordered life of the Church after Christ's bodily Ascension,' whereas Gregory's Homily 9 expounds Matthew 25:14-30 (Parable of the Talents, lines 90-97) and Homily 13 expounds Luke 12:35-40 (lines 139-145), neither of which expounds Mark 13:34's household or doorkeeper (rather, Bede expounds Mark 13:34-37 and borrows Gregory Hom. 9's Ascension image and Hom. 13's threefold Vigilat definition). This leaves the per-Father attribution requirement from iteration 0 unresolved in section 60 and violates guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md (lines 189-190, 235-238) and proper-study/review.md.
findings.required_result: Separate St. Bede's and St. Gregory the Great's exact passages and arguments cleanly at sections/60-lane-vigilant-stewardship.tex:4 and 8 so each Father is credited strictly with what his own witness states. Plain rewrites: (a) line 4: replace 'St. Bede and St. Gregory the Great distinguish clerical and lay watchfulness and map the night watches onto the ages of human life;' with 'St. Bede distinguishes clerical and lay watchfulness in Mark 13:34-37 (drawing on St. Gregory the Great's Ascension and vigilance homilies), while St. Gregory in Homily 13 (on Luke 12:35-40) maps the night watches onto the ages of human life;'; (b) line 8: replace 'St. Bede (In Marci Evangelium Expositio IV.13) and St. Gregory the Great (Homiliae in Evangelia, Homilies 9 and 13) read the household of Mark 13:34 as the ordered life of the Church after Christ's bodily Ascension.' with 'St. Bede (In Marci Evangelium Expositio IV.13) reads the household of Mark 13:34 as the ordered life of the Church after Christ's bodily Ascension, drawing his Ascension image from St. Gregory the Great's Homily 9 (on Matthew 25:14-30) and his definition of watchfulness from Gregory's Homily 13 (on Luke 12:35-40).'

findings.problem: Iteration 1's register-repair audit against the earlier text and controlling records exposes two dropped or altered verification and rights qualifications (a source defect under proper-study/review.md: 'a repair that moves the study's inference into a Father's mouth, or drops a qualification, is a source defect, not a style one'): (1) at sections/30-detailed-commentary.tex:83, iteration 0 bounded the Sacramentarium Veronense XXVIIII.372 comparison to 'the secondary 2002 digital reproduction of the Missale Romanum (pp. 82-83)' and 'secondary-2002 temporali,' matching the verified comparison passage (passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-tertia-2002.english-completion-20261029-postconciliar-phase3-temporal-advent-1-main-prayer-over-the-offerings-all-1-comparison) and the canonical shared Missal owner (verified.md:50-52); iteration 1 dropped that qualification and wrote 'differing in its petition body from the 2002 typical edition only by a single inflection (ancient temporalis against modern temporali),' overstating the witness collated and contradicting sections/20-appointed-texts.tex:81 and sections/90-scope.tex:16 (which state that printed 2002 and printed 2008 correspondence remains unverified); (2) across eight rewritten sentences covering modern Latin Missal prayers, Prefaces, and solemn blessings (30:16, 83, 87, 103, 105; 40:22; 50:24; 60:22), iteration 1 replaced 'withheld under rights limits' or concise 'modern text withheld' with 'withheld under copyright' (including 30:16: 'The modern Latin and English texts of Da, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus ... are withheld under copyright' and 30:83: 'The modern Missal text of Suscipe, quaesumus, Domine ... is withheld under copyright'). This contradicts the controlling rights inventory src/sources/inventories/postconciliar-latin-rights-v1.toml, which records civil_law_status = 'unresolved' and states explicitly that withholding modern Latin Missal text is an operational decision from the absence of an affirmative distribution basis and 'not a civil-law adjudication that copyright subsists in every word' (while ICEL holds copyright on the 2010/2011 English translation and the Holy See claims copyright on the Latin typical editions).
findings.required_result: Restore both qualifications in plain reader prose: (1) at sections/30-detailed-commentary.tex:83, restore the secondary-reproduction bound so the sentence does not claim direct collation against the printed 2002 typical edition (e.g., 'The ancient Roman formula of the Sacramentarium Veronense (Section XXVIIII, marginal 372) preserves its historical antecedent, differing in its petition body from the consulted 2002 digital reproduction of the Missal only by a single inflection, ancient temporalis against temporali.'); (2) replace 'withheld under copyright' at 30:16, 83, 87, 103, 105 and 40:22, 50:24, 60:22 with accurate plain wording matching sections/10, 20, and 90 and postconciliar-latin-rights-v1.toml — for example, 'modern text withheld' (as already used cleanly in 40:8, 50:8, and 60:16) or 'withheld under the rights limits noted in the Scope appendix' where a full clause is needed.

findings.problem: Two sentences in the interpretive lanes project the study's own cross-passage imagery directly into the mouth of a liturgical prayer or biblical/patristic author rather than stating what each source says and marking the synthesis inference plainly (violating guidance/editorial.md, 'Say what the texts say, plainly' and guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md, lines 189-190): (1) sections/40-lane-hidden-presence.tex:8 states that 'in its ancient Gelasian antecedent (II.lxxxiv), the assembly asks almighty God for a willing heart to go out and meet Christ rather than drift into numbness while he tarries.' Direct inspection of Sacramentarium Gelasianum Vetus II.lxxxiv (historical-book-ocr-e4500b54 lines 20493-20499) shows the prayer asks for the will to go forth fittingly in righteous deeds (in operibus iustis aptos occurrere) to meet Christ at his coming; it says nothing about drifting into numbness while he tarries, which is Interpretation 1's own thematic gloss; (2) sections/60-lane-vigilant-stewardship.tex:18 writes 'In the Second Reading (1 Cor. 1:3-9), Paul reminds the household that it lacks no spiritual gift for its post (1:7), while warning implicitly that it must be confirmed "unto the end without crime" (1:8) rather than fracturing the master's house through party quarrels (Chrysostom, Homily II).' Neither 1 Corinthians 1:3-9 nor St. John Chrysostom's Homily II (ccel-text-10a3454d lines 654-920, checked directly) calls the Corinthian church 'the household,' speaks of 'its post,' or calls the assembly 'the master's house'; those metaphors belong to Mark 13:34 and cannot be attributed to Paul or Chrysostom.
findings.required_result: Keep each source's own wording distinct from the study's cross-passage inference. Plain rewrites: (a) sections/40-lane-hidden-presence.tex:8: replace 'in its ancient Gelasian antecedent (II.lxxxiv), the assembly asks almighty God for a willing heart to go out and meet Christ rather than drift into numbness while he tarries.' with 'in its ancient Gelasian antecedent (II.lxxxiv), the assembly asks almighty God for the will to go forth fittingly in righteous deeds to meet Christ at his coming — a petition for active readiness during the long wait.'; (b) sections/60-lane-vigilant-stewardship.tex:18: replace 'In the Second Reading (1 Cor. 1:3-9), Paul reminds the household that it lacks no spiritual gift for its post (1:7), while warning implicitly that it must be confirmed "unto the end without crime" (1:8) rather than fracturing the master's house through party quarrels (Chrysostom, Homily II).' with 'In the Second Reading (1 Cor. 1:3-9), Paul assures the Corinthians that they lack no spiritual gift while awaiting Christ's manifestation (1:7), yet as St. John Chrysostom observes (Homily II), promising to confirm them "unto the end without crime" (1:8) quietly warns a church threatened by party quarrels; read alongside Mark 13:34, Christ's household is already equipped for its work yet cannot afford internal division.'

findings.problem: Two minor citation polish details remain: (1) in sections/10-opening.tex:11 (maptable Entrance Antiphon row), '(Ps. 25[24]:1--3)' is printed redundantly at the end of column 3 even though column 2 already prints '(Ps. 25[24]:1--3)'; (2) in sections/70-comparison.tex:12 (comparisontable, 'Key textual cruxes' row, column 1), '64:1--3b (Descendisti)' uses an en-dash range across the omitted verses Vulgate 64:2-3a, whereas sections/10:13, 20:29, 30:18, and 30:25 distinguish the discontinuous verses precisely as '64:1, 3b' or '64:1 -> 64:3b'. Neither misleads a reader who sees the appointed texts and commentary, so this does not block.
findings.required_result: Remove the duplicated trailing '(Ps.~25[24]:1--3)' from column 3 of sections/10-opening.tex:11, and change '64:1--3b' to '64:1, 3b' in sections/70-comparison.tex:12.

summary: Independent cold review of the Gemini postconciliar expansive study for the First Sunday of Advent, Year B (src/gemini/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s01-first-sunday-of-advent-year-b/main.tex, sections/10-95, generated/scriptural-date-location.tex, proper-components.toml, publication.toml, and research/production-review.md) verified against the sealed research records, controlling rights inventories (postconciliar-latin-rights-v1.toml, liturgical-english-rights-v1.toml), author-standing-v1.toml, and held primary witnesses in src/sources/ (Jerome PL 24 OCR, Aquinas Parma Vol. 14 OCR and Catena Aurea in Marcum 13:32-37, Augustine Enarrationes in Psalmos Ps. 24/79/84 and De gratia et libero arbitrio ch. 45, Bellarmine Explanatio Ps. 24/79/84, Chrysostom Homilies on 1 Corinthians Hom. II, Lapide Vol. 7 OCR, Hilary De Trinitate IX.58-68, Bede In Marci Evangelium Expositio IV.13, Gregory the Great Homiliae in Evangelia Hom. 1/9/13, Cyril of Jerusalem Catechesis 15, Leo the Great Sermon 19, Bernard Sermones in Adventu 3.4 & 5.1, Sacramentarium Gelasianum Vetus II.lxxxiv OCR, Sacramentarium Veronense XXVIIII.372 with secondary-2002 comparison, GIRM 90, Clementine Vulgate, and Douay-Rheims). All seven iteration-0 blocking findings (STU-001 through STU-007) except the remaining Bede/Gregory conflation in section 60, plus advisory STU-008, were repaired cleanly; rights-limited mode matches the production plan and reviewed research, zero copyrighted ICEL/NABRE or modern Missal text is reproduced, and the three interpretations are genuinely distinct and well supported. Consequential-difficulty test outcomes: (1) Isaiah 63:17 and 64:1->3b (Jerome PL 24 cols. 643-646 vs. Aquinas Parma Vol. 14 pp. 370-371) PASS — both witnesses' actual inferences and divergence are accurately taught in sections 30, 40, and 50; (2) 1 Corinthians 1:4-9 (Chrysostom Hom. II §§1-8 and Lapide Vol. 7) PASS — verbatim quotes and lexical/pastoral reasoning on apokalupsis and Fidelis Deus are clear and checked; (3) Mark 13:32-37 (Hilary IX.65/67, Bede IV.13, Gregory Hom. 9/13, Augustine Ep. 199 via Catena Aurea) PASS in sections 30 and 40, but FAIL on patristic attribution in sections/60-lane-vigilant-stewardship.tex:4, 8. Three study-owned blocking source/attribution defects remain (all inside REVIEW_SCOPE): STU-009 (conflating Bede IV.13 and Gregory Hom. 9/13 in section 60), STU-010 (register-repair drops of the secondary-2002 digital comparison bound at 30:83 and an overbroad 'withheld under copyright' legal claim on modern Latin Missal texts contradicting postconciliar-latin-rights-v1.toml across 30, 40, 50, and 60), and STU-011 (projecting editorial cross-passage wording into the Gelasian antecedent at 40:8 and into Paul/Chrysostom at 60:18), plus one minor advisory (STU-012). Disposition: CHANGES_REQUIRED.
